newsitem.title: USA: Rain slows Arkansas cotton, grain, soy harvests.
newsitem.headline: Rain slows Arkansas cotton, grain, soy harvests.

text.p: Below normal temperatures and rain early in the week followed by a freeze slowed Arkansas harvest progress during the week ended Sunday, said the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
Three days were suitable for fieldwork.
Soybeans were 58 percent harvested versus 81 a year ago and the five-year average of 65. The crop was rated 16 percent excellent, 42 good, 29 fair, 11 poor and two very poor.
Cotton was 84 percent harvested versus 90 a year ago and the 81 average. The crop was rated eight percent excellent, 55 good, 34 fair and three poor.
Cotton harvest and ginning progressed in several counties. The Dumas Cotton Classing Office reported 441,250 bales classed as of October 31.
Winter wheat was 36 percent emerged and 48 planted versus 41 and 72, respectively, a year ago and the 43 and 62 five-year averages.
Rice was 100 percent harvested versus 100 a year ago and the 98 average. Sorghum was 99 percent harvested versus 100 a year ago and the 98 average.
Oats were 72 percent planted versus 39 a year ago and the 65 average.
Soil moisture was rated 46 percent surplus, 50 adequate and four short.
